articles.title: ‘I will let my bat do the talking’: Mukul Choudhary on handling pressure, absorbing advice at LSG
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Mukul Choudhary isn’t one to dwell on selection twists.
articles.body: JAIPUR: Mukul Choudhary isn’t one to dwell on selection twists. The 22-year-old wicketkeeper-batter from Jhunjhunu has this season endured a turbulent domestic campaign marked by bizarre selection calls. After an ankle injury saw Sumit Godara replace him in the first game, a fully fit Mukul was entirely omitted from Rajasthan’s second Ranji Trophy match. The shuffling peaked when he was named for the third match, only to be abruptly replaced by Vishal Harsh the next day and relegated to the Under-23 setup.True to form, the Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) finisher responded emphatically, smashing 112 off 129 balls against Mumbai in his first CK Nayudu Trophy game. He was then handed the U-23 captaincy after original skipper Himanshu Nehra was promoted to the senior squad, only for the selection dynamics to pivot again on Saturday with his own inclusion into Rajasthan’s T20 squad for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.After leading the U-23 side to an outright victory over Bihar on Friday, Mukul is now home for Diwali. In a candid chat with TOI, the youngster reflects on his whirlwind journey, tactical growth, and an off-season developmental stint in the UK, remaining focused on letting his bat do the talking.Mukul admits he never anticipated fetching a massive deal of Rs 2.6 crore. “I never thought I’d command such a price tag,” he says. “My domestic season was going well, and after performing in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2025-26, my confidence grew. A couple of franchises, specifically MI and RCB, called me for trials. So while I knew some team might pick me, I certainly didn’t expect to secure such a substantial contract.”Interestingly, his path to LSG was entirely unpredictable. “LSG didn’t hold trials for me. There was no prior contact or discussion,” Mukul reveals. “I didn’t even realize I was on their radar, let alone expect to join them.”Breaking into the playing XI required treating internal practice matches like qualifiers. “When I joined, there was an open slot in the middle order,” he shares. “Our batting coach was Lance Klusener and he told me directly: ‘For you, the practice matches are your selection matches. Play them with that mindset if you want to make the final XI.’ I was the highest run-scorer across all three practice matches, even won one game single-handedly. That paved my way into the side, which is no small feat for an uncapped player.”The road wasn’t smooth. Recalling early missed opportunities, Mukul says, “I was dismissed for just 16 in my first game, and in the next match, I missed two or three full tosses. Even though we won, I went back to my hotel room feeling completely dejected. At this level, you rarely get second chances.”A critical turning point came right before a crucial clash against Kolkata Knight Riders, a match where he would go on to smash an unbeaten 27-ball 54, including seven sixes. In the lead-up to the game, the then LSG skipper Rishabh Pant noticed him batting too cautiously in the nets.“I was batting quite defensively,” Mukul remembers. “Rishabh bhai noticed it and intervened. He told me, ‘What are you doing? Express yourself and play your natural game... We believe in you, you will get your opportunities, and you have to back yourself to deliver.’ Later, on the team bus, he called me over and reinforced that confidence.”That dugout backing allowed him to play with complete freedom, contributing to a famous win.Addressing his tactical progress, Mukul keeps his cards close to his chest. “I won’t share all the technical details,” Mukul smiles. “There are a couple of finisher-role specifics I am adding, figuring out how to develop even better scoring shots that can help the team when it matters most.”Once the IPL season concluded, LSG arranged for him to travel to the UK, where the coaching staff, including Justin Langer, ran camps in Manchester. “The UK experience was great because the wickets are different, and pace bowlers get more help there,” he notes. “Adapting to those conditions helped refine my game.”To maintain momentum, Mukul regularly trains at the Coaching Beyond Academy in Chennai under former India bowling coach Bharat Arun and G Jaikumar, the newly appointed batting coach for LSG. “Working under minds like Bharat Arun sir and Jaikumar sir at the Chennai academy has been incredible for my development,” Mukul adds.Whether talking about his domestic grind or shifting formats, Mukul’s focus remains singular. “Be it LSG or Rajasthan, or red-ball or white-ball, the goal is to win matches for the team. You cannot let success alter your intensity. I just want to keep scoring runs, prove myself every single day, and let the bat do the talking,” the youngster says.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Late release, upright seam, heavy ball: Decoding Mohammed Shami’s sorcery
articles.summary: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami.
articles.body: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami. The fast bowler from a nondescript village in Uttar Pradesh’s Sahaspur, which literally translates to the “land of courage”, bowled with a big heart, indefatigable spirit, and unmatched skill over 64 Tests.Former England captain Alastair Cook’s dismissal during the Visakhapatnam Test in 2016 was a case in point. Shami bowled a series of outswingers that forced Cook to play away from his body. On cue, he then delivered a perfect inswinger that jagged back sharply to sneak past Cook's defence and cannon onto the stumps.“It’s all in those beautiful wrists,” Shami’s childhood coach Badruddin Siddiqui told TOI.“The reason for his success was that he released the ball late and did not rush through his action. This helped him extract late swing off the track. With those malleable wrists, he made subtle changes at the point of release that batters found hard to pick,” the coach demystified Shami’s skill set.Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. Shami was also a bit of a paradox because of the ability to make the old ball skid low while also hurling the ‘heavy ball’ that flew past the batter’s nose.The ‘heavy ball’ — the delivery that pitches shorter and reaches the batter quicker than expected, and hits the bat with extra force despite bowling from a relatively smooth, upright run-up — became Shami’s calling card on numerous overseas tours.The 2018 Johannesburg Test was a classic example: he dismantled South Africa, cruising at 124/1, for 177 to hand India a landmark 63-run win. Shami finished with figures of 5/28, unleashing his trademark ‘heavy ball’ on the spicy Wanderers pitch.At times, he could be erratic even when the conditions were loaded in his favour. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy.Shami was also a great senior, who passed on his art and tricks of the trade to youngsters.“I learnt a lot of things from him during my time in the IPL. Subtle things like bowling at the death and with the semi-new ball,” Uttar Pradesh pacer Ankit Rajput said.At 36, Shami had been performing admirably in this Ranji season, picking up 14 wickets in his last three games. Yet, the constant snubs and time away from international cricket had hurt him.“He was trying hard to make a comeback. But after a point, he realised he was not going to get another chance in Tests, which is why he chose to retire,” Badruddin explained.“He wants to play the ODI World Cup next year. He has kept that window open,” he added. Shami is India’s highest wicket-taker in the 50-over World Cups, with 55 scalps from 18 games at an impressive average of 13.5.The sorcerer of seam signs off from Tests, leaving a gaping hole in India’s bowling roster. Finding Shami’s replacement would be as difficult as locating Sahaspur on the India map.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia cricket: Usman Khawaja says he has not 'thrown anyone under the bus' with claims about ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja says he made "promise" to friend David Warner that he would tell the truth about the 'Sandpapergate' scheme; former Australia batter says he initially wanted to come clean in 2018 but was talked out if by Steve Smith; Khawaja's claims come ahead of release of his book
articles.body:
Batter Khawaja, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, said he had made a "promise" to David Warner - one of three players banned in the wake of 'Sandpapergate', along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft - that he would "tell the truth".

The bowling attack for the Cape Town Test - Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood - released a statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot, while Cricket Australia has always asserted only Smith, Warner and Bancroft knew about it.

Khawaja said in a video on Instagram: "I haven't ⁠thrown anyone under the bus.

"The guys ‌that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we're ‌not the victims.

"[Bancroft, Warner and Smith] took the blame for all of us, and they're the victims - people telling them that they're cheats, getting nailed by the crowd, public humiliation.

"I made a promise to my childhood friend David Warner that I would tell the truth, so he could tell a story. I'm absolutely 100 per cent unapologetic for that. These three guys deserve justice and I haven't pointed fingers at anyone.

"I'm still searching for what I was searching for all those years ago. For us, me included, to take the blame together as a team, so we can all move on from this once and for all.

"You know what? I would do it again in a heartbeat."

Khawaja: Smith talked me out of coming clean

Khawaja said he wanted to come clean in 2018, only to be talked down by Smith, and then again in 2021 after Bancroft said in a newspaper interview that it was "probably self-explanatory" that the bowling attack were aware of the ball-tampering scheme.

The 39-year-old said: "[Smith] being the man and leader he was talked me out of it. He wanted to take the blame. I argued but he was having none of it. That's the first time I tried to come out."

On wanting to fess up five years ago, only to then feel he couldn't once Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon issued their statement, Khawaja added: "I wasn't going to go to war with those guys back then. I just wasn't comfortable. That's the truth.

"How was I ever supposed to bring this up when I knew some of my team-mates didn't want to talk about it? I knew everything I did or said influenced and affected the team.

"I was always conscious of putting my team first. What I say now isn't a reflection of them anymore. Now my words don't influence the team at all. I speak for myself."

Bancroft keen to 'move on' from ball-tampering saga

Another of Khawaja's claims was that fellow batter Bancroft had volunteered to use sandpaper on the ball in the game before the infamous Cape Town Test, which took place in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha.

Bancroft - who has only made two appearances for Australia since 'Sandpapergate', both in the 2019 Ashes, and recently said he accepted a Test return was unlikely at this stage of his career - is keen to "move on" from the ball-tampering story, according to his Beau Casson, his coach at state side Western Australia.

Speaking after Bancroft scored 32 for WA against England in Perth , as the tourists warmed up for a three-match ODI series against Australia from Friday, Casson said: "The situation's a long time ago. He's keen to move on and let his bat do the talking.

"You can't control everything. The way he's handled it, over the past couple of weeks, and over the years gone by, it speaks volumes of the way he's done that.

"He certainly sets the example of how to go about being a professional cricketer."

articles.title: IPL 2027 trade tracker: Complete list of all player and cash deals before the IPL 2027 mini-auction
articles.summary: Stay updated with the live IPL 2027 trade tracker. Get the complete list of all official player swaps, cash transfers, and salary details before the mini-auc...
articles.body:
Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants complete blockbuster swap involving Rishabh Pant and Kuldeep Yadav.

Pant returns to Delhi on a reduced fee; Kuldeep moves to Lucknow at the existing price.

Hardik Pandya's MI exit rumoured, with KKR and Rajasthan Royals interested.

Every IPL trade update ahead of the 2027 mini-auction

Franchises across the Indian Premier League are inching closer to finalising their retention lists for the 2027 season, with the mini-auction scheduled for December.

Before that auction window opens, several teams are expected to explore trade routes first, swapping players outright or settling deals purely in cash, as a quicker way to patch up squad gaps before bidding even begins.

Over the years, several marquee names, including Hardik Pandya, Robin Uthappa and Cameron Green, have switched franchises through trade deals rather than the auction table. Pandya's switch from Gujarat Titans to Mumbai Indians remains the benchmark example of how dramatic these moves can get.

With that history in mind, here's where things currently stand on both confirmed and rumoured trades heading into the 2027 cycle.

Completed trades so far before IPL 2027 mini auction

Net effect of the swap: CSK loses ~INR 2.20 crore, SRH gains ~INR 9.20 crore

The biggest move so far has already been signed off by the IPL governing council, a direct swap between Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants.

Rishabh Pant makes his way back to Delhi, the franchise where he spent nine seasons and featured in 111 matches between 2016 and 2024.

He joins DC at a reworked salary of INR 15 crore, a sharp drop from the INR 27 crore LSG had paid to sign him at the 2025 mega auction.

Going the other way, left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav exits Delhi after a five-year stint to link up with Lucknow, retained at his existing price tag of INR 13.50 crore.

Because the two salaries don't match up exactly, the swap also shifts purse space between the franchises, with LSG picking up roughly INR 13.75 crore in extra room while DC loses close to INR 1.25 crore to fund Pant's revised deal.

Delhi conducts another trade, sends T Natarajan to SRH

T. Natarajan has been welcomed back at SRH after his trade away from DC, with leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari going to the Capitals.

Natarajan represented SRH for five seasons from 2020 to 2024. He was picked by DC at the mega-auction for INR 10.75 crore and now goes at SRH for a revised fee of INR 5 crore.

Ansari featured in 10 matches for SRH in IPL 2025 and picked up 6 wickets. He joins DC with the same fee of INR 40 lakhs and will fill in the gap left by Kuldeep Yadav in DC's spin attack.

CSK & SRH complete 4-player swap deal involving Livingstone & Ellis

Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad have completed a four-player swap ahead of IPL 2027. CSK have acquired Liam Livingstone for ₹6 crore and Jack Edwards for ₹3 crore, while Khaleel Ahmed (₹4.8 crore) and Nathan Ellis (₹2 crore) move to Hyderabad.

Livingstone, bought by SRH for ₹13 crore at the last auction, managed only 15 runs in two games in IPL 2026 before losing his place.

CSK gain middle-order power and spin options, with Edwards adding seam cover. Hyderabad strengthen their bowling, with Khaleel returning to a former franchise and Ellis being a handy customer at the death overs.

Major player trade rumours before IPL 2027 mini auction

1. Could Hardik Pandya be on the move again?

While the DC-LSG swap is done and dusted, attention has now turned to growing chatter around Hardik Pandya's future at Mumbai Indians.

Reports suggest Kolkata Knight Riders have reached out to MI's management to gauge interest in a possible trade, while Rajasthan Royals are also said to be circling.

CSK is also reportedly eyeing a swap deal that could see Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre moving to MI and they get Pandya in a trade. MI, though, have denied every trade rumour thus far .

As per journalist Rohit Juglan , Pandya to KKR is highly possible as the journalist claimed that the all-rounder is unlikely to move to CSK.

On October 21, a popular MI fan account posted that three IPL franchises are reportedly interested in acquiring Hardik Pandya via trade from the Mumbai Indians. They listed three teams: RR, CSK and KKR in the race.

On November 3, Cricbuzz reported that MI are in a decisive stage of trade next and the "next 48 hours" could be crucial. It linked Hardik to PBKS for a direct swap for Arshdeep Singh. Another team was RR, where it would be a swap for Yashasvi Jaiswal, with the option of including Ravi Bishnoi as well.

On Saturday, reports emerged that MI and PBKS are on the verge of completing a trade deal involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh. The move will be made official in the next 24 to 36 hours.

There are whispers of a potential trade involving Sam Curran and Romario Shepherd , one that could see Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals swap the two all-rounders.

Meanwhile, Kolkata Knight Riders are reportedly showing early interest in Suryakumar Yadav , with the franchise eyeing him as a potential future leader for the side.

4. RR to offer Yashasvi Jaiswal to MI for Pandya?

According to reports, Rajasthan Royals are reportedly planning to send Yashasvi Jaiswal to Mumbai Indians as part of a swap deal to sign their captain Hardik Pandya ahead of the IPL 2027 campaign.

5. Chennai Super Kings and Gujarat Titans explore Urmil Patel swap

Chennai Super Kings and Gujarat Titans are reportedly in discussions over a potential trade involving young wicketkeeper-batter Urmil Patel. Reports suggest Patel could make the move to Gujarat, with Chennai potentially receiving either Washington Sundar or Sai Kishore in return as part of the arrangement.

6. RCB and Rajasthan Royals weigh Shepherd-Curran trade

A separate rumour links Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals in a possible swap involving West Indies all-rounder Romario Shepherd and England's Sam Curran.

7. Gujarat Titans and Punjab Kings discuss Wadhera-Brar exchange

Gujarat Titans and Punjab Kings are reportedly exploring a deal that would see batter Nihal Wadhera move to Gujarat, while pacer Gurnoor Brar could head in the opposite direction to Punjab Kings.

8. Gujarat Titans turn down Hardik Pandya over captaincy demands

According to The Indian Express, Pandya had reached out to GT for a potential reunion, but the franchise had to turn him down due to his captaincy demands.

9. Abhishek Sharma seeks SRH exit after Ishan Kishan named captain; franchise issues denial

Sunrisers Hyderabad are in a spot of bother as explosive opener Abhishek Sharma has reportedly expressed a desire to move on, disgruntled over the franchise's decision to hand the captaincy reins to Ishan Kishan.

The leadership snub has evidently left Abhishek disillusioned, and The Times of India has reproted that he has held exploratory talks with heavyweights like Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Titans, with Delhi Capitals and Punjab Kings also keeping tabs on the situation. However, the SRH CEO has categorically rejected the rift as "not true".

10. Rohit Sharma may take MI captaincy back from Hardik Pandya

According to India Today , Mumbai may turn to Rohit once more, a development that puts the spotlight on Hardik's future and on the club's long-term plans.

However, contrary to the speculation, NDTV has reported that there have been 'no internal discussions' in the Mumbai camp about Rohit being appointed as the next captain. The NDTV report was quoting an unnamed source in the franchise.

According to Revsportz, Axar Patel could join Chennai Super Kings in a trade deal from Delhi Capitals. On November 8, CSK themselves fuelled the trade rumour as they posted a photograph of Axar Patel with Ruturaj Gaikwad.

According to Cricbuzz , Rajasthan Royals and Lucknow Super Giants are discussing a potential multi-player trade involving three or four players, with the deal agreed upon in principle.

RR are reportedly keen to acquire an LSG fast bowler, with a spinner also potentially included, while Lucknow could receive one or two RR batters or all-rounders to address their batting weaknesses.

The players involved have not yet been identified, with the two franchises reportedly working towards finalising the deal ahead of the November 17 retention deadline.

On November 7, reports emerged that Lucknow Supergiants are strongly linked with a move for Yashasvi Jaiswal as the India opener seems set to leave Rajasthan Royals ahead of the IPL 2027 campaign.

articles.title: Usman Khawaja: I have not thrown anyone under the bus with relevations
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja says he has "not thrown anyone under the bus" with revelations about the sandpaper scandal that engulfed the Australia team in 2018.
articles.body:
Usman Khawaja said he has "not thrown anyone under the bus" with revelations about the sandpaper scandal that engulfed the Australia team in 2018.

In his autobiography - Sabr - and in an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald, Khawaja claimed the entire team should take responsibility for the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in the third Test against South Africa eight years ago.

At the time, the only players punished were captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft.

Speaking in videos posted on Instagram on Sunday to clarify his comments, Khawaja said: "You would have seen when I mentioned it was all of us, that's implying that whether we like it or not, we are all responsible for what happened together.

"As a team, we need to take that collectively. That is all.

"But now that everyone's talking, am I going to deny that everyone knew? Nah, I won't deny that, either. But I never speak on behalf of anyone else in my book, contrary to what the headlines in clickbait media would have you think."

Other players involved in the Cape Town controversy have repeatedly denied involvement or knowledge of the plot to alter the condition of the ball by rubbing it with sandpaper.

Four bowlers who played for Australia in that Test - Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon - remain part of the team. Cummins has been Test captain since 2021.

In 2021, the quartet released a joint statement which said they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".

On Saturday, Darren Lehmann, the Australia coach who resigned in the wake of the ball-tampering scandal, also denied Khawaja's claims when he told ABC: "I don't think everyone would have known."

Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. He scored 6,229 runs in 88 Tests for Australia.

In October, it was revealed that Khawaja had met with Cummins to discuss the contents of the upcoming autobiography.

That meeting took place before Australia's recent Test series in South Africa, which the Proteas won 2-1.

In the videos on Instagram, 39-year-old Khawaja explained that blame for the plot should have been shared among the entire set-up, not only Smith, Warner and Bancroft.

"I waited till the [South Africa] series was over. And you know what? I haven't thrown anyone under the bus," Khawaja said.

"The guys that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we're not the victims.

"These three guys took the blame for all of us, and they're the victims. Yes, it was tough for everyone, including me. I had sleepless nights, too."

Khawaja also defended not revealing his version of the sandpaper saga at the time, or following the bowlers' statement in 2021, and instead waiting for his autobiography.

"You ask why didn't I say anything in those four years after that while I was still playing? You know what? I never wanted to be the first guy to chat about this," he said.

"Call me a chicken or whatever you want, I didn't know how to do it because I was still on the team. How was I ever supposed to bring this up when I knew some of my team-mates didn't want to talk about it?"

Cricket Australia is yet to indicate a desire to re-open the investigation into the events at Newlands in 2018.

A statement from the governing body said: "There has been a great deal of speculation in the eight years since the 2018 Cape Town Test, including extensive media coverage throughout last month's series in South Africa.

"During this time there has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case. All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process."

Rodrigues' century took Mumbai to the Super League stage of the tournament.Returning from a four-month layoff from the game due to a hamstring injury, Rodrigues had scored 58 off 41 balls against Delhi and 26 not out off 19 balls against Uttar Pradesh in a nine-over game."Jemi's century yesterday was quite good, because the ball wasn't coming nicely on the bat. There was low bounce, it wasn't a flat pitch, but she placed the ball well, piercing the gap between two fielders, instead of trying to hit the ball hard. She played very smartly; it was a smartly built innings, as, realising the nature of the wicket, she didn't want to go for big shots. She came to bat in the fifth over of the innings and started off with two paddle sweeps, which got her two twos, and then gave us the necessary momentum. She paced her knock well and got to her century in the last over," Mumbai Women's team head coach Ajay Kadam told TOI.Interestingly, despite being the Delhi Capitals captain, Rodrigues wasn't the Mumbai skipper in the league stage of the tournament, as she joined the team late. Mumbai were captained by Manali Dakshini. "Jemimah was fine with that. She has no issues with that. She's a team player," Kadam said.Praising the impact of Rodrigues on the team, Kadam said, "Jemimah has definitely added a lot of energy to our dressing room. She has gained vast experience by now. Her presence matters a lot. The girls look up to her. She joined the team after a few matches, but since then, has played her role very well. She has lifted the team to a whole new level, given them confidence. She is a star."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who is Arjun Rajput? The left-handed batter who came to India's rescue against Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Under-19 batter Arjun Rajput came to his team's rescue with a brilliant century against Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup on Sunday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Under-19 batter Arjun Rajput came to his team's rescue with a brilliant century against Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup on Sunday. The youngster from Jalandhar showed great composure when India were struggling at 22/3 after choosing to bat first at the Ministry Turf 1.Rajput walked in at No. 5, with the team desperately needing a partnership. However, Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, could score only 22 off 40 balls. Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, also failed to make a significant contribution.With wickets falling at the other end, Rajput took responsibility and played attacking cricket. He used sweeps against spinners and played aerial shots against fast bowlers to put pressure back on Pakistan.He scored 107 off 85 balls, hitting 11 fours and five sixes, before getting dismissed. His innings helped India reach 208 before being bowled out in 46.3 overs.Who is Arjun Rajput?The 18-year-old from Jalandhar, Punjab, received his first call-up to India's Under-19 team in July this year. He had an impressive run in the 2026-27 Under-19 Vinoo Mankad Trophy, where he scored 695 runs in eight innings and helped Punjab win the title. He also scored an unbeaten 55 off 33 balls in the final.Rajput had earlier made headlines playing for Ludhiana Lions in the Sher-E-Punjab T20 Cup, where he smashed 78 off just 46 balls against Mohali.Cricket runs in his passion, but his family background is a humble one.The youngster's journey to the India U-19 team has been shaped by years of hard work and family sacrifices. His father, Hoti Ram, initially earned a living by selling chhole-kulche from a roadside cart in Jalandhar.He later moved to a small bakery, from where he continues to prepare and deliver kulchas.Speaking about his son's journey, he told NDTV Sports, “I have been making kulchas for many years. Arjun has been playing cricket since the age of five years. He is very talented and hardworking.”Rajput began training at the Harbhajan Singh Cricket Academy before continuing his development under coach Vikram Sidhu.He also contributed with the ball against Nepal in India's tournament opener, taking three wickets for just eight runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Hamza Zahoor's century overshadows Arjun Rajput's 107 as Pakistan U19 pull off thrilling three-wicket win over India
articles.summary: Pakistan Under-19 pulled off a memorable three-wicket victory over arch-rivals India in the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026, with captain Hamza Zahoor
articles.body: Pakistan Under-19 pulled off a memorable three-wicket victory over arch-rivals India in the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026, with captain Hamza Zahoor producing a composed century to guide his side home in a tense chase at Al Amerat, Oman, on Sunday.Chasing 209, Pakistan found themselves in deep trouble at 63/5, with India's bowlers threatening to take the game away. However, Zahoor held his nerve and led a remarkable recovery, stitching together a crucial 107-run partnership with Hasnain Abbas Dar to turn the contest around.Dar contributed 38 off 67 balls before departing at 168/6, giving India another opening. But Zahoor continued to anchor the chase, eventually taking Pakistan across the finish line with three wickets to spare.The result handed Pakistan an important Group A victory over their traditional rivals and strengthened their position in the race for a place in the semi-finals.Arjun Rajput's fighting century rescues IndiaEarlier, India endured a disastrous start after captain Lakshya Raichandani was dismissed for a duck in the first over. Pakistan's pace attack kept the pressure on, reducing India to 42/4 and then 86/5.With the top order back in the pavilion, Arjun Rajput took responsibility and launched a counter-attack. The left-hander smashed 107 off 85 deliveries, striking 11 fours and five sixes, to give India a fighting total.Rajput found useful support from Anvay Dravid (10) and Manal Chauhan (11), but his dismissal at 170/7 in the 36th over triggered another collapse. India lost their remaining wickets for 38 runs and were bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs. Kavya Patel's 23 provided a late contribution, helping India cross the 200-run mark.Pakistan bowlers keep India under controlPakistan's bowling unit played a major role in restricting India to 208. Ali Raza led the attack with three wickets, while Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq also claimed three wickets apiece. The early strikes from Raza and the pressure maintained by Mohammad Sayyam put India on the back foot, before the spinners tightened their grip in the middle overs.India fight back but Zahoor stands firmIndia did not make Pakistan's chase easy. Manal Chauhan picked up two wickets, while Kavya Patel and Mohit Ulva also struck as Pakistan slipped to 61/5. But Zahoor's partnership with Dar changed the course of the match. Even after Dar's dismissal, the Pakistan captain remained in control and completed the job, sealing a three-wicket win for his side.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kavem Hodge's unbeaten 140 puts West Indies on brink of series sweep after Towhid Hridoy's 242
articles.summary: Kavem Hodge put West Indies firmly in the driver's seat with a commanding unbeaten century as the visitors tightened their grip on the second and final
articles.body: Kavem Hodge put West Indies firmly in the driver's seat with a commanding unbeaten century as the visitors tightened their grip on the second and final Test against Bangladesh in Dhaka on Sunday. Backed by valuable contributions from Kevin Wickham and Brandon King, Hodge guided West Indies to 345/3 at stumps on Day 4, stretching their overall lead to 315 runs and leaving Bangladesh with a daunting task to avoid a series whitewash.With just one day remaining, West Indies are well placed to dictate terms and push for a clean sweep after having already taken control of the contest. Bangladesh's bowlers struggled to find answers against a West Indies batting line-up that showed patience and aggression in equal measure.Hodge remained unbeaten on 140, while Amir Jangoo was batting on 20 when bad light brought an early end to proceedings.Hodge leads West Indies' charge with unbeaten centuryResuming the day at 7/0, West Indies made a confident start as King and Joshua Da Silva put together an 85-run opening partnership. The stand was eventually broken by Taijul Islam, who produced a sharp delivery to trap Da Silva leg-before for 36.King continued to look comfortable at the crease and brought up his sixth Test half-century. However, his promising innings came to an end when he attempted an aggressive shot against off-spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz and was dismissed for 61, leaving West Indies at 119/2.Bangladesh briefly sensed an opportunity after picking up two wickets in quick succession, but Hodge and debutant Wickham ensured the momentum remained with the visitors.Hodge took on the Bangladesh spinners with confidence, using his feet effectively and finding the gaps with well-timed sweeps. He brought up his third Test century off 142 deliveries, sweeping Taijul towards square leg for a single.Debutant Wickham makes another valuable contributionWickham continued his impressive debut Test with a fluent 78, adding crucial runs alongside Hodge after Bangladesh had made inroads into the West Indies batting order.The youngster brought up his second half-century of the match off 68 balls, striking a boundary through extra cover. Having scored 61 in the first innings, Wickham looked well on course for another significant contribution before chipping a delivery straight back to Taijul, who took a return catch to dismiss him for 78.The dismissal ended a crucial partnership and gave Bangladesh some relief, but Hodge continued to dominate as West Indies moved closer to an imposing total.Taijul was the pick of Bangladesh's bowlers with figures of 2/118, while the rest of the attack struggled to contain the visitors.Bangladesh face uphill task after Hridoy's historic double centuryEarlier in the match, Towhid Hridoy produced a remarkable unbeaten 242 to help Bangladesh recover from a difficult position and post 386 in their first innings. His knock gave the hosts a 30-run lead after West Indies had been bowled out for 356.Hridoy's innings was particularly significant as he became only the fourth Bangladesh batter to score a Test double-century, joining Mushfiqur Rahim, Tamim Iqbal and Shakib Al Hasan.Despite his extraordinary effort, Bangladesh now face the prospect of a challenging final day as West Indies look to build an even bigger lead before declaring. Hridoy believes Bangladesh can still make a contest of the match, stressing that a strong start will be crucial if they are set a target in the region of 350 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We were 20-30 runs short': India U19 captain Lakshya Raichandani on defeat against Pakistan
articles.summary: India Under-19 captain Lakshya Raichandani admitted his side failed to put up a competitive total after Pakistan pulled off a remarkable three-wicket
articles.body: India Under-19 captain Lakshya Raichandani admitted his side failed to put up a competitive total after Pakistan pulled off a remarkable three-wicket victory in their ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup Group A clash in Oman on Sunday. Despite Arjun Rajput's fighting century, India could not capitalise on a promising recovery, allowing Pakistan to chase down 209 with 11 balls to spare.Pakistan were in serious trouble at 61/5 before Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten 100 off 108 deliveries. His composed knock, supported by Hasnain Abbas Dar's valuable 38, turned the contest around and handed Pakistan their second consecutive victory in the tournament.Speaking after the match, Raichandani acknowledged that India were at least 20-30 runs below a competitive total and rued the lack of partnerships around Rajput's innings.'We were 20-30 runs short': Raichandani admits India's batting failureIndia, who elected to bat after winning the toss, suffered an early collapse and were reduced to 42/4. Rajput then took charge with a magnificent 107, keeping India's innings together and helping them recover from a difficult position.However, the Indian captain felt the team could have added significantly more runs had another batter stayed with Rajput for longer."Yeah, they weren't enough. We were 20-30 runs short, but overall there were some good innings from Arjun and a good contribution from KP (Kavya Patel). It was a really good innings, and if someone had stayed there with him (Arjun), it could have been a little bit more total," Raichandani said during the post-match presentation.India eventually folded for 208 in 46.3 overs, leaving their bowlers with a target that Pakistan managed to overhaul despite losing five wickets early in the chase.Raichandani admits India could have bowled betterThe India skipper also conceded that his bowlers missed opportunities to finish the job after putting Pakistan under considerable pressure. Pakistan were struggling at 61/5, but Zahoor and Dar combined to rebuild the innings and shift the momentum in their team's favour. Raichandani felt India could have been more clinical during that phase."Yeah, definitely. We will try to rectify it, and there was a lot of positive from this game. We will try to take that forward. There were some really good efforts. They were 60 for 5. We could have bowled a little bit better, but overall, it was really good," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Everyone knows how to play on a green wicket': Kusal Mendis backs Sri Lanka batters to tackle Pakistan's pace challenge
articles.summary: Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis is confident his experienced batting line-up has the technique and temperament to counter Pakistan's expected pace-friendly
articles.body: Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis is confident his experienced batting line-up has the technique and temperament to counter Pakistan's expected pace-friendly conditions as the visitors prepare for the opening Test in Rawalpindi on Monday. With the hosts potentially opting for a greener surface to bring their fast bowlers into the contest, Mendis has backed his senior batters to rise to the challenge, insisting their experience of playing in England will hold them in good stead.The Sri Lankan skipper believes the presence of experienced campaigners such as Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva, alongside himself, gives the team the necessary confidence to negotiate challenging conditions away from home."We know they will be giving a little bit different wicket. I think the batters have to manage our skills and preparation well. I know we have a very good batting line-up with some very senior players... Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva, myself, and a couple of other guys."Everyone knows how to play on a green wicket. We played really well in England also, so I have no doubt in my batting line-up," Mendis told reporters.First Test assignment as captain for Kusal MendisThe Rawalpindi Test will mark Mendis' first assignment as Sri Lanka's Test captain after he took over the leadership from Dhananjaya de Silva in early October. The 31-year-old admitted that leading the side in the longest format was something he was particularly looking forward to, despite the challenges of an extended stay in Pakistan.Sri Lanka have spent more than a month in the country, having arrived for the preceding white-ball assignments. Mendis acknowledged that spending such a long period away from home, largely between hotels and training sessions, had not been easy for the players.However, he said the squad had found ways to keep itself occupied and was now fully focused on switching gears for Test cricket."Honestly, compared to ODIs and T20s, Test cricket is very different. I think everyone mostly likes to play Test cricket. Me as well. I'm very happy to captain in Test cricket," he said."It's not easy, sometimes we stay in the hotel and come to practice and that's it... I think it's a little bit hard to stay one month in a hotel. But we do some stuff in the team room, games and individual things to keep ourselves entertained."Mendis backs experienced bowling attack to deliverSri Lanka are yet to register a Test victory in their two series this year against West Indies and India, but Mendis believes the performances of his bowling unit offer plenty of encouragement ahead of the Pakistan challenge.The skipper pointed to the experience within the attack, highlighting how the fast bowlers have delivered consistently across formats and are equipped to handle the demands of Test cricket.Sri Lanka have several pace options at their disposal, with Asitha Fernando, Lahiru Kumara, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga forming the fast-bowling contingent alongside all-rounder Milan Rathnayake. Left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya will lead the spin department."We have a very balanced side, both with the bowling and batting unit. I think we've done really well in the past couple of tours in the bowling side, and same in one-day cricket. The fast-bowling attack is doing well," Mendis said."We have a very senior bowling unit, the guys have played so many first-class and international matches. Same in the batting, so everyone is ready for tomorrow's game."Mendis praises Pakistan's hospitality and security arrangementsBeyond preparations for the series, Mendis also expressed satisfaction with the arrangements made by the Pakistan Cricket Board during Sri Lanka's extended stay in the country.The Sri Lankan captain praised the security arrangements and said the players had been comfortable with the local food, which he felt was similar to the cuisine back home."Security-wise, everybody is very happy. Food, we normally eat spicy and everything, so same like in Sri Lanka it's in Pakistan. I think everyone has had a happy stay in Pakistan," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohsin Naqvi's PCB backs Mike Hesson to continue as Pakistan's Test coach
articles.summary: Pakistan's white-ball head coach Mike Hesson will continue to look after the country's Test team as interim head coach until the end of the current World
articles.body: Pakistan's white-ball head coach Mike Hesson will continue to look after the country's Test team as interim head coach until the end of the current World Test Championship (WTC) cycle.Hesson took charge of the red-ball side during Pakistan's difficult tour of England two months ago, after former coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was removed midway through the series.A source in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirmed it to Indian news agency PTI that Hesson had agreed to continue in the role and would also guide the team during next year's Test series against New Zealand."Hesson will also be interim head coach for next year's Test series against New Zealand. The board and head coach have both conveyed this to the players as well," the source said.Hesson's future with Pakistan cricketHesson joined Pakistan as white-ball head coach in May 2025 before taking temporary charge of the Test team. However, his long-term future with the PCB will be reviewed after next year's World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia."Hesson's association with Pakistan cricket will be reviewed after next year's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. It will also then be decided who will be the head coach of the Test side for the next cycle of the World Test Championship," the source added.Questions over Hesson's influenceHesson has become a controversial figure in Pakistan cricket, with several former players and experts questioning the amount of authority he has been given by the PCB, particularly in team selection and other cricketing decisions.Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam also recently admitted that he does not have a say in selection matters. He said his responsibility is to make the best use of the 15-16 players selected by the team management and selection committee.The PCB source also acknowledged that chairman Mohsin Naqvi has great faith in Hesson and trusts him with important cricketing decisions. However, Hesson's frequent changes to the team and players across formats have not gone down well with everyone in Pakistan cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi to stay back for India’s Test preparations
articles.summary: India pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi will remain with the team for preparations ahead of the Test series against New Zealand, batting
articles.body: India pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi will remain with the team for preparations ahead of the Test series against New Zealand, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed on Saturday.The three pacers will stay back after the ODI series as the team begins its preparations for the red-ball challenge.Speaking at the press conference ahead of the third ODI, Kotak said the conditions in the ongoing ODI series had provided useful preparation for the Test matches, particularly for the bowling unit."Both pitches had seam and swing. Good preparations for the Test because the ball will change, but one-day cricket does give you an idea about the conditions. The thickness of the grass and everything. It's been challenging but good for the team and preparations," Kotak said.He also pointed to the three India A matches as an important part of the build-up, saying they had ensured adequate preparation for both batters and bowlers.India's Test players are scheduled to begin a preparatory camp on November 11. Kotak expects the sessions to help the squad get ready for the series."India Test players will start their camp from the 11th, so hopefully those five-six sessions will help get prepared for the Test series," he said.Providing details of the team's immediate plans, Kotak confirmed that head coach Gautam Gambhir would remain with the ODI squad, while he and bowling coach Morne Morkel would travel to Wellington."Gurnoor, Arshdeep and Nabi will stay back for Test preparations. Gambhir stays back with the ODI team, me and Morne will go to Wellington. That's the plan for now," he said.'KL Rahul has played unbelievable innings'Kotak also spoke about KL Rahul's importance to the Indian batting line-up, praising his adaptability and ability to deliver according to the team's requirements.Rahul remained unbeaten on 26 during India's rain-affected chase of 135 in the second ODI. With wickets falling at regular intervals, the wicketkeeper-batter held one end together as India reached 113/7 in 26 overs before rain brought the contest to an end."Biggest advantage is he opens in Test cricket. He is someone who plays according to the need of the team. Since I have joined, he has played unbelievable innings. Never looks under pressure and has never let the team down. Can rotate and can easily hit sixes," Kotak said.On India's approach to playing additional all-rounders, the batting coach said team selection was based on players performing their designated roles rather than making compromises to accommodate an extra batter."We are playing players at the spot. Difficult to reduce a bowler and add a batter," he explained.India take 2-0 series leadMeanwhile, India moved 2-0 ahead in the five-match ODI series after edging New Zealand by four runs under the DLS method in Wellington.Defending a modest target of 135 in a contest reduced to 47 overs per side, New Zealand had India in trouble at 113/7 after 26 overs when rain forced the players off the field. India were four runs ahead of the DLS par score, handing them victory.Gurnoor Brar was the standout performer with the ball, claiming 4/30 in 10 overs, while Auqib Nabi picked up two wickets. Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel also finished with two wickets apiece.Earlier, Daryl Mitchell top-scored for New Zealand with 55, rescuing the hosts from 53/5 through a 59-run partnership with Mitchell Santner, who contributed 31.India will now head to Hamilton for the third ODI on Tuesday, looking to extend their advantage in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
